title: Trailing-CRLF precondition: doc and implementation disagree
description:
header_typed.rs:174-177 — parse_header_typed doc:

    "raw_value is the bytes of the header field value — the portion to the
    right of the `:` in the header line, including any folded continuation
    lines but excluding the header name and the trailing CRLF."

Implementation at lines 213-236 handles three cases for the trailing line ending:
  1. `raw_value` ends with b"\r\n" — used as-is.
  2. `raw_value` ends with b"\n" — converted to b"\r\n".
  3. `raw_value` has no trailing line ending — b"\r\n" appended.

The doc says "excluding the trailing CRLF" — telling the caller they MUST NOT include CRLF. The implementation accepts both. The accepted contract is wider than the documented one. A caller who reads the docs and strips CRLF gets the same result as a caller who passes the field body with CRLF. The two agree, but the documented requirement is a precondition the implementation does not enforce or signal.

Caller-facing consequence: which is the canonical input shape? If a future maintainer (correctly, per the docs) starts treating trailing CRLF as a malformed input signal — e.g., as a marker for "the caller passed the whole header line including the line ending" — they will silently change behavior for callers who relied on the implementation's lenient acceptance. Right now there is no way to tell which usage is "correct".

Fix: either (a) tighten the doc to match the implementation ("trailing CRLF is permitted and stripped"), or (b) document a hard precondition and reject input with trailing line endings explicitly. Without alignment, the contract is fuzzy.
close_reason: Documentation batch on the typed header surface: (.7) parse_header_typed now states trailing CRLF is permitted-but-not-required (matching the implementation); (.8) EmailAddress.name and AddressGroup.name field docs now state the trim+empty-to-None normalization; (.12) HeaderValueTyped doc has a Serde Wire Format section pinning the current externally-tagged shape and explicitly distinguishing it from RFC 8621 wire format (callers responsible for that mapping); (.17) parse_header_typed doc now carries one runnable example per HeaderForm variant (six total); (.24) HeaderDateTime has an Equality Semantics section noting derived PartialEq is field-wise not instant-wise, with a worked example and the to_timestamp escape hatch; (.25) EmailAddress has an Equality Semantics section noting derived PartialEq is byte-exact (no RFC 5321 domain case-folding) and pointing callers at manual canonicalisation; (.30) parse_header_typed doc has an Empty-Result Ambiguity table making explicit that callers cannot distinguish malformed-vs-empty-vs-non-UTF-8 and flagging the future-direction (strict variant / warnings tuple). No code changes.
